flawed_step: Lines 9–10: from n+i being at most lcm(1,…,k), the proof treats this as contradicting n≥lcm(1,…,k). Equality is possible.
counterexample: Take k=3 and n=lcm(1,2,3)=6. The interval [6,9] is {6,7,8,9}. Only 7 has a prime factor greater than 3, but the theorem claims at least k+1−π(k)=4−2=2 such integers. At i=0, n+i=6 has greatest prime factor 3 and no prime power divisor greater than k, directly falsifying the claim in line 9.
assessment_summary: The theorem fails at the permitted boundary n=lcm(1,…,k); the proof overlooks the equality case.
